text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Turkey's first Islamist Prime Minister, Necmettin Erbakan, stepped down on Wednesday.
- An Islamist group of companies, Kombassan Holding, is cornered by a court decision to freeze more than $100 million worth of its accounts and securities.
MILLIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel will begin talks with opposition leaders to find an alternative government.
- Two Islamist deputies resign from Erbakan's Welfare Party.
- Kombassan Holding will be monitored by German police for its activities in Germany.
HURRIYET
- Demirel has not immediately appointed former Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller as caretaker to form the next government.
- Central Bank governor Gazi Ercel criticises populist policies pursued by the former Islamist-led government.
YENI YUZYIL
- Opposition leaders will present an alternative government formula to Demirel.
- Sales of cement increase by 10 percent as a halt to demolishing shanty towns is expected in a possible early election.
RADIKAL
- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal is a key name in the formation of the next government.
CUMHURIYET
- Environmentalist group Greenpeace report accuses Turkey and other Mediterranean countries of turning the region into a nuclear weapon warehouse.
DUNYA
- Turkey's name is not even mentioned in plans for European Union expansion.
ZAMAN
- A revamped coalition headed by Ciller is expected to dispel tension in the country.
